newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Bahrain tells Gulf states drop rows, boost economy.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain tells Gulf states drop rows, boost economy.

text.p: Bahrain's prime minister urged Gulf states in remarks published on Wednesday to "freeze" differences and focus on economic cooperation.

"Gulf states can put aside the aspects of their political differences...or freeze them and concentrate on the economic aspect," al-Seyassah newspaper quoted Sheikh Khalifa bin Sulman al-Khalifa as saying in an interview.

Sheikh Khalifa, who is a brother of Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa, did not specify the differences or mention Bahrain's long-standing territorial dispute with fellow Gulf Arab Qatar.

Bahrain is the smallest and least wealthy member of the political and economic alliance the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which also groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

"Prosperity alone will lead to the spread of security and stability," Sheikh Khalifa said. "Intentions should be good in the future...We do not have a way other than to go in this direction to achieve high growth rates."
In reference to unrest in the island state, mainly among Bahrain's Moslem Shi'ite majority, he said: "The situation is good and as desired. The situation...is comfortably stable."
Around 28 people have been killed in two years of sporadic unrest and hundreds of people have been arrested in Bahrain.
